chapter_title: There is no Joy that shall remain in the World till the End.
chapter_note: An exceptionally pure substrate chapter. The entire teaching maps the luminaries' perception of cosmic conditions (the Enemy's rule, the soul's captivity) and the eschatological resolution. Both sides of every mapping stay firmly within the cosmic system. The two-fold enumeration (¶3-4) is classic substrate pedagogy. No editorial bridges, no institutional content, no exhortation to audience. The only non-substrate element is the dialogue frame formula in ¶1. Negative editorial fatigue confirms teaching dominance throughout. The chapter preserves a compact, self-contained cosmological teaching about the incomplete joy of luminaries during mixture.

paragraphs.core_text: There is not [o]ne person [existing in] the world, standing firm [i]n mixture, for whom joy remains to the end.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue frame formula 'Once again he speaks to his disciples:' — standard editorial attribution.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Clean division: formulaic dialogue frame attribution followed immediately by a cosmological principle about mixture. The teaching statement itself is impersonal and systematic.

paragraphs.core_text: Not only people, even the sun and the moon, the light-givers of the heavens, [ ... ] nor are they oppressed, they know not [ ... s]et firm in a summons and an [obe]dience. Nevertheless, they too, they do not rejoice completely.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Extends the cosmic principle from persons to luminaries. The sun and moon are described as cosmic agents ('light-givers of the heavens') set in a summons and obedience — their station within the cosmic architecture. Both sides of the mapping are internal to the system. Lacunae suggest lost material that may have further described their cosmic condition.

paragraphs.core_text: So, one: Their eyes stare at their enemy, they [perceiv]e him and also look at his ugly shapes. They [s]ee him, that he is alive and established and is king above and below, in secret and manifest. He does every thing that he wants according to his wil[l].
paragraphs.temporal_note: First enumeration unit ('one:'). The Enemy is described in cosmic-structural terms: 'king above and below, in secret and manifest' — a spatial-ontological description of his dominion within the system. 'Ugly shapes' is zoomorphic-register description of the dark powers. No side of the mapping leaves the cosmic system.

paragraphs.core_text: [The s]econd: They perceive the living soul, they see [i]t and that it is ensnared and set in a great [fetter] above and below, in the tree and in the flesh, [ ... ] with every oppression. It is being pressed, drawn near to [and] sliced and eaten as it comes up and down; from above below and from below above. It [is] despoiled and moved from body to body.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Second enumeration unit. Dense cosmic-process vocabulary: 'ensnared', 'fetter', 'pressed', 'sliced and eaten', 'moved from body to body'. The soul-body binding and transmigration formula ('moved from body to body') is a substrate marker. 'In the tree and in the flesh' describes the soul's entrapment in the vegetable and animal kingdoms — cosmic domains, not contemporary institutions. The parallel 'above and below' structure echoes ¶3.

paragraphs.core_text: Now, because of their living soul that is loved by them and honoured of them, when they see it in oppression th[ey can] not [re]joice completely.
paragraphs.temporal_note: 'Now' here is a logical connective within the teaching, not an editorial bridge marker. The paragraph draws a causal connection between the luminaries' love for the soul and their incomplete joy. Both sides remain cosmic: luminaries perceiving the soul's condition.

paragraphs.core_text: So, one about the soul; and one about their enemy whom they see ruling [in] what is not his own. He is proud and satisfied with a wealth that is not his own. Indeed, due to this, they do not rejoice in total; but bear up and swallow their heart until they cleanse the living soul and take it from the enemy's hands. Then they obliterate the death that is their enemy and they gather it in [and fetter it in the lump] for ever and ever.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Recapitulation and cosmic-process conclusion. The recapitulation ('one about the soul; and one about their enemy') is structural, not editorial — it closes the enumerated teaching. The process vocabulary is substrate: 'cleanse the living soul', 'obliterate the death', 'fetter it in the lump'. The lump (βῶλος) is a technical cosmological term for the final prison of Darkness. The minor exhortation score (3.45) comes from 'for ever and ever' but this is a cosmological-temporal formula here, not devotional closure.

paragraphs.core_text: When they will chain their enemy in the bond at the [las]t, then they will rejoice and no longer grieve from this t[ime]. Also, they become the very same as they were from the [start] for ever!
paragraphs.temporal_note: Eschatological closure within the cosmic system. 'Chain their enemy in the bond' parallels ¶6's 'fetter it in the lump'. 'They become the very same as they were from the start' is the restoration principle — return to the primordial state before mixture. This is a cosmic-temporal statement (from the start / for ever), not devotional exhortation. The chapter closes with the cosmic cycle complete.
